items.title: Wind, Water, Earth — Then Mount Sumeru Itself

items.zh: 自此以後，有大風輪，量等三千大千世界，從下而起，與彼世界作所依持，為欲安立無有宮殿諸有情類。此大風輪有二種相。謂仰周布及傍側布，由此持水令不散墜。次由彼業增上力故，於虛空界金藏雲興。從此降雨，注風輪上。次復起風，鼓水令堅，此即名為金性地輪。上堪水雨之所激注，下為風颷之所衝薄。
items.en: From this point, a great wheel of wind arises from below, equal in extent to a great trichiliocosm, to serve as the support for that world, so as to provide a dwelling-place for those beings who have no palace of their own. This great wheel of wind has two aspects — one spreading upwards, one spreading outward to the sides — by which it holds water so that it does not disperse and fall away. Then, through the dominant force of beings' karma, clouds bearing a treasury of gold arise in empty space, and rain falls from them, pouring down upon the wheel of wind. Then wind arises again, churning the water until it becomes solid; this is called the golden wheel of earth. Above, it bears the pouring rain and water; below, it is buffeted by the force of the wind.

items.zh: 此地成已，即由彼業增上力故，空中復起諸界藏雲，又從彼雲降種種雨。然其雨水，乃依金性地輪而住。次復風起，鼓水令堅。即由此風力所引故，諸有清淨第一最勝精妙性者，成蘇迷盧山。此山成已，四寶為體。所謂金、銀、頗胝、琉璃。若中品性者，成七金山。
items.en: Once this earth is formed, through the dominant force of beings' karma, clouds bearing the treasury of the elements again arise, and various rains fall from them. This rainwater rests upon the golden wheel of earth. Then wind arises once more, churning the water until it becomes solid. Through the force of this wind, whatever is of the purest, most excellent, most refined nature becomes Mount Sumeru. Once this mountain is formed, it has four precious substances as its substance: gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli. Whatever is of a middling nature becomes the seven encircling gold mountains.

items.title: Mount Sumeru and the Seven Gold Mountains, Measured

items.zh: 謂持雙山、毘那矺迦山、馬耳山、善見山、朅達洛迦山、持軸山、尼民達羅山。如是諸山，其峯布列，各由形狀差別為名，繞蘇迷盧次第而住。
items.en: [The seven gold mountains are named:] Yugandhara, Vinataka, Aśvakarṇa, Sudarśana, Khadiraka, Īṣādhara, and Nimindhara. These mountains, their peaks arrayed in sequence, are each named for their distinctive shape, and stand encircling Mount Sumeru in order.

items.zh: 蘇迷盧量，高八萬踰繕那，廣亦如之，下入水際、量亦復爾。又持雙山，等彼之半。從此次第，餘六金山其量漸減，各等其半。
items.en: Mount Sumeru measures eighty thousand yojanas in height, the same in breadth, and the same again in depth beneath the water's surface. Yugandhara measures half of this. From there in sequence, each of the remaining six gold mountains measures half again of the one before it.

items.title: The Four Continents, and the Lower Realms

items.zh: 若下品性者，於蘇迷盧四邊七金山外，成四大洲及八中洲，并輪圍山。此山輪圍四洲而住，量等尼民達羅之半。復成非天宮殿，此宮在蘇迷盧下，依水而居。復成大雪山及無熱池周圍崖岸。次成最下八大那洛迦處，諸大那洛迦，及獨一那洛迦、寒那洛迦、近邊那洛迦。復成一分鬼、傍生處。
items.en: Whatever is of the lowest grade, beyond the seven gold mountains surrounding Mount Sumeru, becomes the four great continents, the eight intermediate continents, and the encircling ring of mountains. This encircling mountain surrounds the four continents, measuring half of Nimindhara. There also forms the palace of the asuras, situated beneath Mount Sumeru, resting upon the water. There also form the great snow mountains and the cliffs surrounding the Lake of No Heat. Next form the eight great hells at the very bottom, together with the great hells, the solitary hells, the cold hells, and the neighbouring hells. There also forms a portion of the realms of hungry ghosts and animals.

items.zh: 四大洲者，謂南贍部洲、東毘提訶洲、西瞿陀尼洲、北拘盧洲。其贍部洲，形如車箱；毘提訶洲，形如半月；瞿陀尼洲，其形圓滿；北拘盧洲，其形四方。贍部洲量，六千五百踰繕那；毘提訶洲量，七千踰繕那；瞿陀尼洲量，七千五百踰繕那；拘盧洲量，八千踰繕那。
items.en: The four great continents are: Jambudvīpa in the south, Pūrvavideha in the east, Aparagodānīya in the west, and Uttarakuru in the north. Jambudvīpa is shaped like a cart's box; Pūrvavideha is shaped like a half-moon; Aparagodānīya is perfectly round; Uttarakuru is square. Jambudvīpa measures 6,500 yojanas; Pūrvavideha, 7,000; Aparagodānīya, 7,500; and Uttarakuru, 8,000.

items.title: Seas, Dragons, and the Guardians of the World

items.zh: 又七金山，其間有水、具八支德，名為內海。復成諸龍宮。有八大龍，並經劫住。謂持地龍王、歡喜近喜龍王、馬騾龍王、目支隣陀龍王、意猛龍王、持國龍王、大黑龍王、黳羅葉龍王。是諸龍王，由帝釋力，數與非天共相戰諍。其諸龍眾類有四種。謂卵生、胎生、濕生、化生。妙翅鳥中，四類亦爾。復有餘水，在內海外，故名外海。
items.en: Further, between the seven gold mountains lies water endowed with eight excellent qualities, called the inner seas. There also form the palaces of the dragons — eight great dragon kings, who dwell there for the full duration of the eon. Beyond the inner seas lies yet more water, called the outer sea.

items.zh: 又依蘇迷盧根，有四重級。從蘇迷盧初級，傍出一萬六千踰繕那量。即從此量，半半漸減，如其次第，餘級應知。有堅手神住最初級，血手神住第二級，常醉神住第三級，持鬘神住第四級。蘇迷盧頂四隅之上有四大峯，各高五百踰繕那量。有諸藥叉，謂金剛手止住其中。
items.en: Further, resting on the base of Mount Sumeru there are four tiers. From Sumeru's first tier, it extends outward sixteen thousand yojanas; from there, each subsequent tier's extent is halved in turn, and so on for the remaining tiers. The spirit Sthirahasta dwells on the first tier, Raktapāṇi on the second, Sadāmatta on the third, and Mālādhara on the fourth. At the four corners of Sumeru's summit stand four great peaks, each five hundred yojanas high, where the yakṣas — headed by Vajrapāṇi — dwell.

items.zh: 又持雙山，於其四面有四王都。東南西北隨其次第，謂持國、增長、醜目、多聞四大天王之所居止。諸餘金山，是彼四王村邑部落。
items.en: Further, on the four sides of Yugandhara stand the capitals of the Four Heavenly Kings: in the east, south, west, and north, in order, dwell Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa, the four great heavenly kings. The remaining gold mountains serve as the towns and villages of these four kings' domains.

items.zh: 又近雪山，有大金崖，名非天脅，其量縱廣五十踰繕那，善住龍王常所居鎮，又天帝釋時來遊幸。此中有樹，名曰善住，多羅樹行，七重圍繞。復有大池，名漫陀吉尼，五百小池以為眷屬。善住大龍與五百牝象前後圍繞，遊戲其池，隨欲變現，便入此池，採蓮花根以供所食。

blocks.text: Today's reading builds the physical world from the bottom up: a wheel of wind, a wheel of water, the golden earth, Mount Sumeru at the centre, seven rings of gold mountains, four continents, seas, dragons, and the Four Heavenly Kings. It is the classical Buddhist map of the world. Read it as the treatise intends, as the shared result of beings' karma, and do not worry about memorising the measurements. The commentary picks out what our teachers stress.

One passage is untranslated (0287b04–b11): near the Himalaya is a great golden cliff called "the Asuras' Flank", fifty yojanas square, where the dragon-king Supratiṣṭhita lives and which Indra sometimes visits, with a tree called Supratiṣṭhita surrounded by seven rows of palm trees and a great lake called Mandākinī with five hundred small lakes around it.

Beneath everything is a great **wheel of wind** (風輪), with two aspects, "one spreading upwards, one spreading outward to the sides", by which it holds the water above it so that it does not fall away. Clouds then rain upon it, forming the **wheel of water**; the water is churned by wind until its surface hardens into the **golden earth**, as cream forms on boiled milk. On it, by further winds, the mountains and continents arise.

Venerable Miào Jìng clarifies two names for the clouds. 金藏雲, "metal-treasury cloud", is cloud containing metallic matter. 諸界藏雲, "elements-treasury cloud", is cloud containing the four elements, earth, water, fire, and wind. (Ru-Yi's earlier rendering of these two was corrected after the question bank noticed it.)

subs.head: Mount Sumeru and the seven gold mountains

blocks.text: **Mount Sumeru** (蘇迷盧, *Sumeru*) is made of four precious substances, gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli, and measures eighty thousand yojanas in height, the same in breadth, and the same again below the water. Around it stand seven concentric ranges of gold mountains, each half the height of the one inside: Yugandhara (持雙), Īṣādhara (持軸), Khadiraka, Sudarśana (善見), Aśvakarṇa (馬耳), Vinataka, and Nimindhara.

They are "each named for their distinctive shape", with one exception noted by Venerable Miào Jìng, following Kuījī: Vinataka, "Obstacle", is named for a spirit on the mountain who obstructs good practice.

subs.head: Four continents, and the realms below

blocks.text: Beyond the gold mountains lie the four great continents, each with two lesser continents, ringed by the Iron Mountains (輪圍山):

items: **Jambudvīpa** (南贍部洲), our world, to the south, shaped like a cart's box, narrow at one end and wide at the other;
**Pūrvavideha** (東毘提訶洲) to the east, like a half-moon;
**Aparagodānīya** (西瞿陀尼洲) to the west, round;
**Uttarakuru** (北拘盧洲) to the north, square.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng corrects two common miswritings: the eastern continent is 東勝身洲 ("superior body"), not 勝神洲 ("superior spirit"); and 贍部 takes the shell radical, not the "eye" radical of 瞻.
Below Jambudvīpa lie the hells, and the ghost realm is described too. The cosmology is not only geography; it maps the destinations of beings.

subs.head: Seas, dragons, and the guardians of the world

blocks.text: Between the gold mountains are inner seas of water with eight good qualities; beyond them, the salt ocean. Dragon palaces form, with eight great dragon-kings who live through the whole eon. On the four sides of Yugandhara stand the capitals of the **Four Heavenly Kings** (四大天王), the guardians of the world: Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the east, Virūḍhaka in the south, Virūpākṣa in the west, and Vaiśravaṇa in the north. Familiar statues in Chinese temple gates represent exactly these four.

Why include all this in a treatise on yoga? The two teachers' answer, from Day 8, holds throughout: these are the shared fruits of beings' karma, and so the work of the mental consciousness. The scale is meant to humble. Our own lives and our own world are one small instance within an immense, karmically ordered whole.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what two aspects does the great wheel of wind at the world's base have, and what do they do?
options: cold and hot, regulating climate
moving and still, making the world turn
upper and lower, separating heaven and earth
spreading upwards and spreading outward to the sides — by which it holds water so that it does not disperse and fall away
quiz.why: "This great wheel of wind has two aspects — one spreading upwards, one spreading outward to the sides — by which it holds water so that it does not disperse and fall away." Master Cháng Bǎi: one blows upwards, one outward, so the water does not scatter and fall. Venerable Miào Jìng compares the wind wheel, loosely, to today's atmosphere.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what four precious substances make up Mount Sumeru?
options: gold, silver, bronze, and iron
pearl, agate, coral, and amber
gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli
the seven treasures
quiz.why: "Once this mountain is formed, it has four precious substances as its substance: gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli." A gives the wheels of the four wheel-turning kings in §54. §36 matches each substance to a continent: lapis lazuli facing Jambudvīpa, silver Pūrvavideha, gold Aparagodānīya, crystal Uttarakuru. Venerable Miào Jìng: the finest grade of matter forms Sumeru, the middling forms the seven gold mountains.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are Mount Sumeru's dimensions?
options: ten thousand yojanas high, five thousand below water
eighty thousand yojanas in height, the same in breadth, and the same again in depth beneath the water's surface
eighty thousand high, forty thousand below water
sixty thousand high
quiz.why: "Mount Sumeru measures eighty thousand yojanas in height, the same in breadth, and the same again in depth beneath the water's surface." Venerable Miào Jìng: "eighty thousand above the water, eighty thousand below." C's forty thousand is Yugandhara, "half of this." On the length of a yojana, Master Cháng Bǎi lists three figures: forty li by old tradition, thirty by Indian custom, sixteen in Buddhist reckoning.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what shape is each of the four great continents?
options: Jambudvīpa like a cart's box, Pūrvavideha like a half-moon, Aparagodānīya round, Uttarakuru square
all four are round
Jambudvīpa round, Uttarakuru a half-moon
Jambudvīpa square, Pūrvavideha like a cart's box
quiz.why: "Jambudvīpa is shaped like a cart's box; Pūrvavideha is shaped like a half-moon; Aparagodānīya is perfectly round; Uttarakuru is square." Venerable Miào Jìng cites Kuījī: an Indian cart-box is narrow below and wide above, just as Jambudvīpa is wide in the north and narrow in the south. Their measures are 6,500; 7,000; 7,500; and 8,000 yojanas.

quiz.q: Where do the Four Heavenly Kings dwell, and which one is in the east?
options: on Sumeru's summit; Vaiśravaṇa in the east
in the sea; Virūḍhaka in the east
on the encircling ring; Virūpākṣa in the east
on the four sides of Yugandhara; Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the east (Virūḍhaka south, Virūpākṣa west, Vaiśravaṇa north)
quiz.why: "On the four sides of Yugandhara stand the capitals of the Four Heavenly Kings: in the east, south, west, and north, in order, dwell Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa … The remaining gold mountains serve as the towns and villages of these four kings' domains." The four peaks of Sumeru's summit in A are home to the yakṣas under Vajrapāṇi; the summit's centre holds Śakra's palace. Master Cháng Bǎi likens the whole arrangement to a concentric watch guarding the world's axis.
